messages:
Maya Patel: pinging the thread for visibility — customer FinchDev opened an escalation (C-4382) about streaming disconnects when using our gRPC gateway + HTTP/1.1 proxies. They see partial outputs, client reconnect storms, and billing spikes. posting logs and repro below.

FinchDev (customer): hey team — we have multiple customers reporting that when our clients call the /v1/stream chat endpoint via a gRPC->HTTP1 gateway, the stream ends abruptly. sometimes we get the last token, sometimes not. clients reconnect and re-send the same prompt which doubles token usage. started around 2026-11-02 14:00 UTC after we rolled a new gateway image.

Maya Patel: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro request and the gateway config?

FinchDev (customer): reproducer:
```
# client -> gRPC gateway -> redwood
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://gateway.example.com/v1/stream?model=redwood-mini" 
```
Gateway is Envoy 1.26 with gRPC-JSON transcoder enabled, and a sidecar NGINX that terminates TLS and proxies to Envoy.

FinchDev (customer): sample client log (truncated):
```
> recv: data: {"delta":"Hello"}\n

> recv: data: {"delta":" world"}\n

# then suddenly:\n

> recv: [connection closed by peer]
```
No final event with done/status. Reconnects immediately.

Rajat Singh: hmm this smells like HTTP/2 trailer headers (grpc-status / grpc-message) are getting lost when the gateway translates h2 -> h1. many HTTP/1 intermediaries (or misconfigured Envoy filters) drop trailers or buffer the body until stream close. If the translation drops trailers, client doesn't get final status and sometimes treats the stream as incomplete.

Lina Gomez: can you share a server-side request id from the same session? we have dropped-trailer logs in runtime that increment trailer_missing metric, but it's rare.

FinchDev (customer): request id: req-20261102-48a3 (attached request logs). Also saw a 502 from nginx right before disconnect in the edge logs.

Maya Patel: copying eng-runtime (Lina) and infra (Rajat). initial triage checklist:
- exact client User-Agent + SDK version
- gateway/transcoding config (Envoy filters)
- TLS termination topology (you said nginx + envoy)
- reproduce with curl via gateway (no SDK) to rule out client recon logic
- check runtime logs for trailer_missed or partial_write errors

FinchDev (customer): UA: FinchSDK/2.4.5 (node) — reproduces with curl too. I can give a short window access to staging to run tests.

Lina Gomez: quick theory: gRPC uses HTTP/2 trailers to convey final grpc-status. When the gRPC->HTTP1 gateway converts the response, if it sends a 200 with chunked body but doesn't map trailers to a final JSON chunk (or omits them), the client that expects SSE or gRPC semantics will think stream ended prematurely. some proxies also rewrite Transfer-Encoding and strip trailers.

Rajat Singh: confirming — Envoy has known issues when using certain filter chains with the grpc_json_transcoder + HTTP/1.1 upstream. If Envoy sees an upstream HTTP/2 response with trailers, and the upstream is connected via HTTP/1.1, it may buffer and then close without propagating trailers downstream. The buffering might cause partial payloads to be flushed in odd chunk boundaries too.

Maya Patel: customer impact: partial outputs -> visible in UI, then clients resend -> duplicate token charges -> billing spike. Also customers report higher p95 latency (requests that reconnect end up with two half responses).

Lina Gomez: immediate mitigations we can suggest to Finch:
1) Bypass the gRPC->HTTP1 transcoder and talk to Redwood with direct HTTP/1 streaming (our SSE-compatible path) if possible. That avoids trailers.
2) Configure Envoy to preserve trailers: set "use_remote_address: false"? (not exact) — actually the flag is to avoid remote addr issues. More concretely, ensure upstream protocol is http2 in Envoy for the path to Redwood, or set envoy's preserve_trailers option and disable buffering filters (like response_buffer).

Rajat Singh: added: in nginx, ensure proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; and add proxy_set_header Transfer-Encoding "chunked" only if you want chunked. But note: many nginx builds strip trailers. If possible, terminate TLS directly at envoy and avoid nginx proxying trailers.

FinchDev (customer): we pushed a rollback of the new gateway image and rolling back reduced the incidents by ~90% within 20 mins. So likely gateway filter change caused this.

Maya Patel: good signal — please keep staging access open for a repro window. Lina / Rajat can we get a quick runbook for Finch? also need to track telemetry to detect future occurrences automatically.

Lina Gomez: I'll add a runtime metric: streaming.trailer_missing_count and streaming.partial_chunk_count. short-term: we can detect EOF-without-trailer and emit an internal event. Long-term: add a more tolerant client-side framing that tolerates missing trailers by treating stream close as success if final chunk includes "done": true. But that's risky for grpc-style semantics.

Rajat Singh: config checklist to send customer now:
- Envoy: upstream_protocol_options: use_http2: true for the cluster to redwood
- Remove grpc_json_transcoder if not needed for simple SSE
- Disable response buffering filters: response_buffer and/or set max_response_bytes low
- Nginx: proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_buffering off; consider enabling chunked_transfer_encoding on proxied requests

FinchDev (customer): trying the envoy change in staging now. will report back in ~10m. thanks for the pointers.

deploy-bot: deployment finished: envoy-config-rollout v2026.11.02-rc3 -> applied to staging cluster a, b.

FinchDev (customer): quick update — after forcing upstream HTTP/2 to Redwood cluster, streams are stable in staging. no trailer_missing logs. production rollback still in place.

Maya Patel: great. next steps:
- Lina to add short-term alerts for trailer_missing_count > 0 for a customer (>3 in 5m)
- Rajat to prepare a short KB for customers behind gRPC gateways and common Envoy/nginx gotchas
- Finch to schedule a production re-deploy with the envoy config change and verify post-deploy metrics and billing counters

Lina Gomez: noted — will push telemetry change (metric + alert) to canary in the observability cluster. ETA 48h.

Rajat Singh: I'll draft KB and share in this thread.

FinchDev (customer): thanks everyone — appreciate the rapid triage. I'll keep the ticket open and will DM if we see regressions.

Maya Patel: closing the escalation loop here once Finch confirms production deploy. created internal task: INF-1761 to track runtime telemetry and KB writeup.

(End of thread)
